# Top 10 NASDAQ-100 Holdings

| Rank | Company | Ticker | Market Cap | P/E Ratio | % of Index |
|------|---------|--------|------------|-----------|------------|
| 1 | Apple | AAPL | $3.4T | 29.5 | ~12% |
| 2 | Microsoft | MSFT | $3.1T | 36.2 | ~11% |
| 3 | Nvidia | NVDA | $2.9T | 53.8 | ~9% |
| 4 | Amazon | AMZN | $2.0T | 43.7 | ~6% |
| 5 | Meta Platforms | META | $1.3T | 26.8 | ~4% |
| 6 | Broadcom | AVGO | $780B | 54.3 | ~3% |
| 7 | Tesla | TSLA | $750B | 89.5 | ~3% |
| 8 | Costco | COST | $370B | 52.1 | ~1.5% |
| 9 | Netflix | NFLX | $345B | 40.2 | ~1% |
| 10 | Adobe | ADBE | $225B | 40.8 | ~1% |

**Note:** These figures are approximate and based on recent data (early 2025). Market caps, P/E ratios, and index weightings fluctuate daily with stock prices and earnings reports. The NASDAQ-100 is a modified market-cap weighted index.

**Key observations:**
- The top 3 holdings represent over 30% of the index
- Tech mega-caps dominate the index
- P/E ratios vary significantly, with Tesla having the highest valuation multiple
